Adverse hits must be documented and, where required, reported to TRACFIN under the suspicious transaction reporting regime of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) in conjunction with the RCS database search portal (https://data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be expressed in Latin script; French accents are permitted. Non-French names are accepted but must be transliterated into Latin characters in all registration filings and official extracts. Mandatory corporate deeds (statuts) and French legal notices must be in the French language in accordance with French language law (Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) request written reasons from the greffe or INPI; (2) file an administrative appeal before the supervising commercial court (tribunal de commerce) within 30 days of the notification of rejection; or (3) resubmit a modified name directly through the INPI Guichet unique. The initial name reservation may be renewed once upon request to the greffe where local practice permits.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-licensed software/cloud infrastructure SAS. French commercial domiciliation rules allow an SAS to use an authorized domiciliation provider, provided the provider is approved, a written domiciliation contract for at least three months is in place, and official mail can be lawfully received and forwarded. A bare virtual address without legal representation or document forwarding does not constitute a valid registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for low-risk unlicensed IT activities; estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by social, fiscal, or police authorities within the first 24 months is 10-15%, with a 5% probability of UBO-verification inquiry from TRACFIN.

incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be incorporated as a French Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) with a share capital of one (1) Euro. RESOLVED, that the initial share capital be subscribed in full by the sole shareholder in cash. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address specified in the statuts and that the Board of Directors adopt this as the permanent registered office. RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: a Président, a Directeur Général, and any additional directors as required. RESOLVED, that the corporate object shall be to develop, operate, and provide infrastructure, database, and API monitoring cloud services, and to engage in all activities related thereto. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for customs export clearance; corporate taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; single official business-registration one-stop shop: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs clearance portal: douane.gouv.fr / DELTA-D.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated and registered through the electronic Guichet Unique (Article R.123-1 et seq. Code de commerce). Upon validation, INSEE assigns the SIREN/SIRET (official French corporate TIN), the local Greffe registers the company at the RCS, and the assigned SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) issues the French intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) without separate application. Foreign entities not established in France but with direct French taxable supplies must self-register for VAT with the SIE des entreprises non résidentes (non-resident desk of DGFiP, Paris) using the simplified identification declaration and supporting certificate of establishment abroad; no advance tax clearance is required for ordinary cloud/DevTools activity (licence-free sector).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SAS is a limited-liability capital company automatically subject to French Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at 25% standard rate (15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit under qualifying SME criteria), regardless of shareholder composition. Territorial_Scope: France applies the territoriality principle (Article 209 CGI) - IS taxes only profits attributable to French operations or French permanent establishments, while profits booked through foreign permanent establishments are exempt. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable to a mainland-domiciled SAS for ISIC 6201 cloud infrastructure. Pass_Through_Eligible: not available for an SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Fiscal integration election (régime d'intégration fiscale, Article 223 A CGI): a French-resident SAS parent holding at least 95% of voting rights in French subsidiaries may elect group taxation, yielding a single taxable result and immediate set-off of intra-group profits/losses. Parent-subsidiary election (régime mère-fille, Article 145 CGI): dividends on qualifying shareholdings are 95% exempt from IS. No US-style check-the-box election exists in French law; hybrid entity classification follows mandatory ATAD rules transposed in Articles 209-0 A and 212 bis CGI, requiring asymmetric-timing elections to be disclosed on the annual return. Standard annual IS election (option de taxation au réel normal, Article 50-0 CGI) is automatic for the SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT, harmonised under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum threshold for non-established foreign suppliers - French VAT registration and liability arise from the first euro of French taxable supplies (Articles 259, 283 CGI). Domestic small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA): EUR 85,000 for supply of goods; EUR 37,500 for services, including B2B cloud/digitally supplied services. Pan-EU distance-sale and e-services threshold: EUR 10,000 for the Union OSS scheme; B2B supplies of cloud, database and API-monitoring services to French VAT-registered customers are entirely reverse-charged (autoliquidation) at 20%, with no registration required where the supplier's only French activity is such B2B reverse-charge supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing reform (Article 20 loi de finances 2024) as amended: from 1 September 2026, large and mid-size enterprises must issue structured electronic invoices and all taxable persons must accept them; from 1 September 2027, micro and small enterprises must also issue; B2C sales data must be electronically reported (e-reporting) to DGFiP on the same phased timetable. Invoices must flow through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDP) using Factur-X, Universal Business Language (UBL) or Cross-Industry Invoice (CII) XML formats, transmitted by secure API; there is no 'digital stamp' regime, but DGFiP receives invoice datasets in near-real time and uses them for automated VAT pre-filling and cross-referencing with customs and bank data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods destined outside the EU are exempt with credit at 0% under Article 262 CGI, subject to actual removal of the goods from the EU and preservation of probative export evidence. Intra-EU dispatches are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI where the acquirer supplies a valid EU VAT number and the French seller meets declaration obligations (DEB/EC Sales List and Intrastat where applicable). Cross-border B2B cloud, database and API-monitoring services supplied to non-French or non-EU business customers are outside the scope of French VAT (place of supply at the customer's establishment, Article 259-1 CGI); B2C e-services supplied to consumers outside the EU are likewise outside the French VAT base (Article 259 D CGI). Residual input VAT on costs attributable to export/zero-rated or outside-scope sales is creditable under the ordinary TVA credit regime; refund claims are settled by DGFiP upon scrutiny.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane - DAU / DAE) lodged electronically via DELTA-D, evidencing the export declaration number and date of departure from France/EU
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR or carrier postal consignment record proving physical movement of goods out of the EU territory
Commercial invoice, export contract and packing list; for cloud/SaaS offshore services: service contract, usage/billing logs and customer VAT registration certificate (Article 289 CGI documentation)
Inward Remittance Certificate equivalent: bank statement or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the French bank account within the prescribed collection period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating or the outside-scope treatment is claimed without probative export evidence, DGFiP re-assesses the undeclared French VAT at 20% together with statutory interest (intérêts de retard, 0.2% per month compounding) and penalties scaling with culpability: 10% for simple omission (Article 1728 CGI), 40% for deliberate bad faith (mauvaise foi, Article 1729(a)), 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (Article 1729(b)), and up to 100% penalty plus criminal fines (EUR 500,000 and/or 5 years' imprisonment) for false invoices or dissimulation (Articles 1741, 1743 CGI). Retrospective reassessment runs for the ordinary three-year limitation, extended to six years where operations are hidden; the exporter is denied VAT deduction on clawed-back sales and the managing director may face joint civil liability where abuse of right or management fault is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) as national central bank within the Eurosystem; Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as bank and EMI prudential supervisor; Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) as exchange-control and foreign-investment policy authority under the Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the EU fully liberalized capital-movement regime under Article 63 TFEU. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account; no prior exchange-control authorization is required for equity injections, profit repatriation, royalties, dividends, or intercompany settlements. Residual constraints are declaratory and statistical: (i) French banks report balance-of-payments data to the BdF; (ii) transfers to or from non-EEA countries may trigger the Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds (DTF) when the statutory threshold is crossed; and (iii) inbound foreign direct investment in sensitive sectors is screened by DG Trésor, a category that does not cover ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 cloud-infrastructure and developer-tools services. Profit remittance from the SAS is unrestricted once the applicable dividend withholding-tax formalities (EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or double-tax-treaty relief) are completed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender rule or minimum conversion ratio applies in France for export proceeds. Receipts in USD or other foreign currencies may be retained in multi-currency accounts (comptes en devises) or converted into EUR at the company's discretion. There is no statutory repatriation deadline, no forced sale of export currency, and no minimum holding requirement. Only periodic balance-of-payments reporting obligations remain, applied through the intermediary bank or directly to the Banque de France when aggregate non-EEA settlements exceed the applicable ESCB reporting threshold.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for operational cash management; low suitability for statutory treasury functions. ACPR-licensed or EU-passported EMIs/PSPs such as Qonto, Shine, Wise Business, and Revolut Business can provide EUR/USD IBANs, SEPA Credit Transfers, SWIFT MT103 processing, and fully remote digital KYC onboarding without physical presence. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot hold escrowed share capital under a bank-style attestation de dépôt, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, cannot provide credit facilities, and cannot act as an EMIR-eligible FX hedging counterparty. Recommended structure: use an EMI for operational receivables and Stripe_Billing/Mercury_ACH netting, while maintaining a Tier-1 French commercial bank account for capital escrow, daily treasury concentration, and FX derivative execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under Article R. 561-5-1 CMF and ACPR guidance when the bank relies on an ANSSI-certified electronic identification and video-KYC process or on a trusted third-party KYC file. In practice, a French-resident director can open an account without a physical visit if the Kbis, statuts, and UBO declaration are submitted through a certified digital channel; a non-EEA director is frequently required to complete one physical interview at a French branch or at a French consulate, or to provide an apostilled and notarized identity dossier. For an international DevOps/SaaS SAS, the fastest compliant corridor is a dual-bank structure: an EMI for immediate operational account opening without in-person interview, plus a Tier-1 bank corporate desk appointment for the escrow and hedging accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO data mismatch: the bank identifies a U.S. or offshore investor chain with no corresponding entry in the French Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed RBE declaration with certificate of filing; full corporate organigram of each intermediate holding entity; certified share registers and constitutional documents of ultimate shareholders; proof that each ultimate beneficial owner is not a politically exposed person (PEP); notarized passport copies and six months of source-of-funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value non-EEA capital injection flagged for source-of-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Two years of audited financial statements of the investing entity; executed share-subscription or shareholder-advance agreement; bank statement showing the wire originating from the investor's own account; tax-residency certificate of the investor; detailed business plan and a capital-utilization budget for the SAS treasury.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA director without French tax domicile or physical presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized passport; proof of residential address (utility bill or lease agreement); six-month personal bank statement; designation of an EEA-based second director or local legal representative; certification from the French company counsel (avocat) confirming the mandate and absence of sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and country-risk screening triggered by a cloud-infrastructure end-user base in restricted or high-risk markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written export-control and sanctions compliance policy; EU/OFSAC consolidated list screening report generated at onboarding; geofencing and IP-routing controls documentation; Stripe and Mercury KYC outputs and merchant-of-record agreements; SOC 2 Type II report; compliance officer letter confirming that ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 services are non-defense, non-dual-use software infrastructure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EU/EEA capital injections: SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR to the SAS FR76-IBAN with a payment reference containing the share-subscription or shareholder-advance contract number; no FX documentation is required beyond the intermediary bank's balance-of-payments purpose code. Non-EEA capital injections: SWIFT MT103 with a valid UETR, full beneficiary legal name matching the Kbis, the investor's registered address, and a purpose code indicating a capital contribution; the receiving bank triggers the Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds (DTF) when the statutory non-EEA threshold is met, and tags the flow for BdF balance-of-payments reporting as 'investissement direct'. If a non-EU investor acquires more than 10% of voting rights or capital, a DG Trésor post-hoc FDI notification is advisable for legal certainty even in the non-sensitive digital-economy sector. Wiring protocol requires the funds to come exclusively from the investor's own bank account, with no third-party intermediary cash accounts, and the SAS must archive the shareholder resolution approving the payment together with the bank confirmation and, where applicable, the DTF receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR vendor and contractor payments: SEPA Credit Transfer settled via TARGET2/T2, using the invoice number as the structured remittance reference; batch execution via the Tier-1 bank or the EMI file upload channel. Cross-border USD/GBP operating disbursements: SWIFT MT103 with cover through MT202 for non-EEA software vendors, infrastructure suppliers, and intercompany payments; USD disbursements inside the United States may use ACH and Fedwire rails through a U.S.-dollar account integrated with Mercury_ACH and Stripe_Billing payout netting. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) are recommended only for physical hardware, colocation equipment, or large-value procurement contracts, with the Tier-1 French bank as issuer. Daily treasury sweeps concentrate all EU and non-EU receivables into the multi-currency concentration account, and standing instructions convert net USD surplus into EUR using the executed FX-hedging line.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) transacted under an ISDA/CSA with a Tier-1 French credit institution, designated in the treasury policy as hedging instruments and eligible for French tax hedge-reserve treatment for the underlying USD revenue stream.
Plain-vanilla FX Options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) to protect the annual budget conversion rate, executed OTC under EMIR with the same ACPR-regulated counterparty.
FX Swaps and Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for rolling USD trade settlements into EUR and for hedging long-dated intercompany financing or capital loans.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under French EMIR-transposing rules for exotic or restricted-currency supplier exposures, but are operationally unsuitable for the EUR/USD pair, which is fully deliverable.
